title: Conjecture 2 (Dvořák and Mnich)
statement_text: There exists a real number $c < 3$ such that every planar graph of girth at least five has fractional chromatic number at most $c$.
context_text: Dvořák, Sereni and Volec [3] conjectured that triangle-free plane graphs without separating 4-cycles cannot have fractional chromatic number arbitrarily close to 3. They remarked that a key step would be to prove this for planar graphs of girth at least five, a special case previously conjectured by Dvořák and Mnich [2]. The present paper's stated purpose is to establish Conjecture 2 for graphs with bounded maximum degree.
paper_contribution: Proves Conjecture 2 for planar graphs of girth at least five with maximum degree at most $\Delta$: such graphs are $(6M_\Delta : 2M_\Delta+1)$-colorable and thus have fractional chromatic number at most $3 - \frac{3}{2M_\Delta+1}$.
paper_title: Fractional coloring of planar graphs of girth five

title: Informal conjecture on improved color ratio in Theorem 5
statement_text: The authors prove that for every triangle-free planar graph $G$ and every vertex $x\in V(G)$, $G$ has a set coloring by subsets of $\{1,\ldots,6\}$ in which every vertex gets at least two colors and $x$ gets three. It might be possible to improve the ratio of extra colors assigned to the vertex $x$ a bit; e.g., it could be true that for every triangle-free planar graph $G$ and every vertex $x$ there exists a set coloring by subsets of $\{1,\ldots,9\}$ such that all vertices get at least three colors and $x$ gets five.
context_text: A set coloring of a graph $G$ assigns to each vertex $v$ a set $\varphi(v)$ of colors so that adjacent vertices receive disjoint sets; $G$ is $(a:b)$-colorable if it has a set coloring by $b$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,a\}$, and the fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ is the infimum of $a/b$ over all $(a:b)$-colorings. By Grötzsch's theorem triangle-free planar graphs are $3$-colorable, and there are triangle-free planar graphs with fractional chromatic number arbitrarily close to $3$. The authors' result with one boosted vertex $x$ (subsets of $\{1,\ldots,6\}$, at least two colors everywhere, three on $x$) implies, by taking the union over all choices of $x$ of colorings with disjoint palettes, that every triangle-free planar graph on $n$ vertices is $(6n:2n+1)$-colorable, so $\chi_f(G)\le3-\frac{3}{2n+1}$; it is also the key step in showing that planar graphs of girth at least five and bounded maximum degree have fractional chromatic number bounded away from $3$. The ratio cannot be improved arbitrarily: if $G$ is the wheel with five spokes with each spoke subdivided once, $x$ is the centre of the wheel, and $\varphi$ is a set coloring by subsets of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ in which every vertex has at least $k/3$ colors, then $|\varphi(x)|\le\frac{k}{3}+\frac{2k}{9}$.
